summary: AE + SE scoped a 4-week POC with Zephyr Cloud to validate ingestion latency and cost/per-token for their search reranking workload. Success criteria: <=10% quality regression vs current model, 95th pct latency < 120ms for tail requests, cost reduction >= 30% on inference unit economics. Timeline: kickoff, access setup, mid-point benchmark, exec readout. Next steps and action items agreed.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Zephyr VP Eng), Tom Greer (Zephyr Platform), Sofia Diaz (Zephyr Security), Ethan Cole (Zephyr Data)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. um this is Maya from Redwood, with Liam our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Aisha: Good, thanks. Busy week but we pulled folks together.
[00:12] Liam: Cool. Quick agenda — scope the POC, confirm success criteria, discuss workload sizing and benchmarks, and agree timeline and milestones.
[00:22] Tom: Sounds good. Our goal is to validate the k-v caching and inference cost on our reranking path, and to see if Redwood Dedicated or a hosted route makes sense.
[00:30] Maya: Right. High level we usually do a 3-4 week POC: kickoff + access, run benchmarks with your sample traffic, mid-point review to tune, and final exec readout. We can flex.
[00:42] Aisha: For success criteria we care about two things: quality (no significant downgrade vs current model) and latency / cost. Specifically, we want <=10% drop in our nDCG and 95th percentile tail latency under 120ms for inference. Cost target is at least a 30% reduction per inference compared to our current infra.
[01:02] Liam: Ok that's clear. A quick question on traffic shape — what qps and typical sequence lengths are we looking at?
[01:09] Ethan: Typical QPS at peak is around 200 with bursts to 350. Most requests are short — prompt tokens ~30, response tokens maybe 60 for reranking context. But some long sessions exist.
[01:22] Liam: Great, that matters for batching and KV cache hit rates. We'll size the benchmark VMs/GPU accordingly.
[01:29] Tom: Also call out security constraints: we need SAML SSO for console access, KMS integration for keys, and SOC2 plus an option for VPC/private deployment.
[01:40] Maya: Yep we support SSO, KMS/HSM integrations, and Redwood Private for VPC deployments. We'll send the security package.
[01:47] Sofia: Please include docs around audit logs and data retention, and any pen test reports you have.
[01:53] Maya: Will do.

[02:10] Liam: For benchmarks we typically run two tracks: functional correctness & quality checks (run your test prompts through model variants) and perf/e2e latency with representative traffic. We'll need: sample request traces, a small eval set for quality, and access to a staging S3 bucket or dataset.
[02:26] Ethan: We can share a 10k example eval set and 1 hour of anonymized request traces. We'll scrub PII.
[02:33] Liam: Perfect. Can you also provide a small set of 'hot' prefixes for caching tests?
[02:38] Tom: Yes we have that.

[03:05] Maya: Timing — we propose kickoff week of 2026-05-25 with an access/setup window of 2-3 days, then week 1 run initial benchmarks, week 2 tune and run mid-point review, week 3 final benchmarks and exec readout at end of week 3 or start of week 4. So roughly 3 weeks.
[03:22] Aisha: That aligns with our internal timeline, we have an exec review slot the week of 2026-06-15.
[03:28] Maya: Good, we'll target that as the readout.

[04:00] Liam: On infra — we recommend starting with a hosted Redwood endpoint to validate quality and latency quickly; if you want isolation and throughput guarantees we can run Dedicated later in the POC or as a parallel run. Some customers run a two-arm test: hosted for quality and Dedicated for throughput/cost.
[04:18] Tom: If we run two arms we need to ensure traceability in metrics, so we can compare apples to apples.
[04:23] Liam: Absolutely, we'll provide a benchmarking harness and scripts to replay traces across both variants.

[05:10] Aisha: A couple of potential blockers: procurement needs a SOW and pricing before we can allocate any budget, and security will need to review the docs before we can allow any data access.
[05:23] Maya: We'll send a draft SOW and a ballpark pricing sheet by end of week. That's on me.
[05:29] Sofia: On security review, who will be our primary contact at Redwood?
[05:33] Maya: Liam will be the SE contact for technical and security questions. I'll be the commercial owner.

[06:00] Liam: For benchmarks - target metrics we should capture: p50, p95, p99 latencies, end-to-end tail latency (client -> response), model quality metrics you use (nDCG/recall), token cost and effective cost per request. Also compute CPU/GPU utilization and batching stats.
[06:18] Ethan: We'll add throughput targets and warm/cold cache scenarios.

[07:00] Tom: Regarding data access, we prefer to grant S3 read-only and temporary IAM creds scoped to a "redwood-poc" prefix. Is that OK?
[07:08] Liam: Perfect, that's what we usually ask for. We'll provide an infra playbook for the exact IAM policy.

[10:00] Aisha: Any recommended model variants? We're currently using an in-house tuned LLaMA variant for reranking.
[10:08] Liam: We'll run a few open variants and a Redwood-verified model that aligns with LLaMA-like architectures; part of the POC is picking the model family that gives the best tradeoff of quality and cost. We'll also test quantized variants to hit your cost target.
[10:25] Maya: Quick note — some transcription systems sometimes garble product names like K-V cache or sometimes say "Redwood Dedicated" as "Redwood dedecated" so apologies if the transcript is messy.

[20:00] (mid-call, more detailed technical back-and-forth)
[20:12] Liam: Walkthrough of benchmark plan: replay harness, step load to peak, run steady-state for 10 minutes at peak qps, measure tail latency. Then run quality eval across eval set and compute rank metrics. We'll also instrument token accounting.
[20:30] Ethan: We'll coordinate to give you an isolated test env or staging S3.
[20:36] Liam: For KV cache we want to run cache-hit experiments with and without prefix caching to see latency benefits.

[35:00] Tom: On success criteria, to restate: nDCG drop <=10%, p95 latency <120ms, cost reduction >=30%. If we hit those we go to exec readout and discuss Dedicated commitments.
[35:16] Maya: Understood. We'll map those to measurable benchmark tests.

[45:00] (late call, procurement and timeline details)
[45:10] Maya: Next steps recap: I'll send SOW + pricing and security docs; Liam will send benchmark plan and infra playbook; Tom/Ethan will provide sample data and traces. Then we schedule kickoff for week of 2026-05-25.
[45:28] Aisha: We'll aim to get procurement and security review started so we can give credentials by 2026-05-18.

[60:00] (wrap up)
[60:05] Sofia: One ask — include a short checklist for security review (SOC2 docs, pen test, encryption in transit & at rest, KMS flow).
[60:15] Liam: Will include that.
[60:20] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone.
[60:25] Aisha: Thanks.
[60:30] Maya: We'll follow up with the materials.

End transcript.

Notes: transcript has small transcription imperfections and occasional mis-attributions; timestamps approximate.
